`XmlValueInstantiator`, where the call to `propDef.getPrimaryMember()` return `null`: The involved code looks roughly like this: ``` public record ObjectId(RepositoryName repositoryName, ItemName itemName) implements ItemId ``` ... with `ItemId` being defined as: ``` @JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME, property = "itemType", include = JsonTypeInfo.As.EXISTING_PROPERTY) @JsonSubTypes({ @JsonSubTypes.Type(value = ObjectId.class, name = "OBJECT"), ... }) @JsonPropertyOrder({ "itemType", "repositoryName", "itemName" }) public sealed interface ItemId permits ObjectId, ... { @JsonProperty RepositoryName repositoryName(); @JsonProperty ItemName itemName(); @JsonProperty(access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY) ItemType itemType(); @JsonIgnore @Deprecated(forRemoval = true) default String getQualifiedItemName() { return repositoryName().value() + ":" + itemName().value(); } } ``` It appears the `qualifiedItemName` property causes havoc despite all attempts to ignore it. (Because it neither present in the serialized XML, nor should it be.) I have already tried - overriding `qualifiedItemName` with `@JsonIgnore String getQualifiedItemName()` in `ObjectId`, - adding an additional `@JsonIgnoreProperties("qualifiedItemName")` in `ObjectId` but with no avail. What appeared to work as a workaround is renaming `getQualifiedItemName` to something without a `get` prefix, which causes the property to not be picked up by Jackson.
